newsitem.title: UK: Congo oil output, exports normal - Elf.
newsitem.headline: Congo oil output, exports normal - Elf.

text.p: Oil production and exports in Congo are normal despite fighting in the capital Brazzaville, an executive of French major Elf Acquitaine said on Tuesday.
"There is no problem in Pont Noire," the executive told Reuters, referring to the Atlantic coast oil export terminal about 400 km (250 miles) west of Brazzaville.
The executive said crude production in the west African country was running at around 250,000 barrels per day (bpd), with exports at around 160,000 bpd, as normal.
Fighters traded heavy gunfire in Brazzaville on Tuesday morning despite an announcement by France of a cease-fire agreement by warring parties.

The militia of former president Denis Sassou Nguesso has been fighting the troops of President Pascal Lissouba for five days in a political and ethnic conflict which began as the country approached a presidential election set for July 27.
Congo's main crude exports markets are the United States and Italy. Elf and Italy's AGIP are the two main concession holders producing Congo's Djeno Blend crude.
